ReductiveGroups — progress on 100 merged pull requests (1f1d752 to ed837d5)

The largest named result of this window is that the character–cocharacter pairing of a split
torus is perfect: for a split torus of finite rank, the dot-product pairing between the character
lattice X*(T) = σ →₀ ℤ and the cocharacter lattice X_*(T) induces isomorphisms onto both
ℤ-duals (TauCeti#1134). It is available both in the coordinate model of the cocharacter lattice
and, transported back, on the genuine lattice of homomorphisms
Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ
(SplitTorus.instIsPerfPair
and instLatticePairingIsPerfPair), with the two non-degeneracy directions proved separately.
Underneath it is the character and cocharacter machinery for a general diagonalizable group D(M)
(TauCeti#968): characters and cocharacters as homomorphisms of group functors, the integer pairing
DiagonalizableGroup.pairing
with its bilinearity, and the power endomorphisms of 𝔾ₘ, which TauCeti#1163 identified with the
canonical integer action on endomorphisms. The roadmap wants the perfect pairing as the input to
root data, and that is exactly where the work stops: nothing here defines a root, a Weyl group, or
a maximal torus sitting inside a larger group, and the perfectness statement is for the split,
finite-rank case only.

Two kernels were computed. μ_n is the kernel of the n-th power endomorphism of 𝔾ₘ
(TauCeti#976,
RootsOfUnityGroup.range_inclusion),
and αₚ is the kernel of the Frobenius endomorphism of 𝔾ₐ (TauCeti#1146,
AlphaP.range_inclusion).
The same pull request builds that Frobenius endomorphism from the observation that xᵖ is
primitive in characteristic p, so x ↦ xᵖ is a bialgebra endomorphism of the coordinate ring of
𝔾ₐ. Both kernel statements are about the functor of points: they are equalities of subgroups of
G(A), natural in the value algebra A, and not scheme-theoretic kernels, which do not exist yet.
αₚ itself arrived earlier in the window (TauCeti#611) with its coordinate Hopf algebra R[x]/(xᵖ),
its points identified with the p-nilpotent elements of A, and
AlphaP.coordinateRing_not_isReduced;
TauCeti#1024 adds that over a reduced algebra it has only the identity point. That is the
roadmap's designated non-smooth example behaving as intended: invisible on reduced points, and not
trivial.

Most of the window, by volume, went into comodules, which the roadmap treats as the engine of
Layer 1. The basic structure landed at the start (TauCeti#62,
Comodule),
and the rest of the window filled in what a working category needs: an R-module of morphisms
(TauCeti#90), preadditivity (TauCeti#106), a zero object (TauCeti#117), binary products carrying
the direct-sum coaction (TauCeti#240), trivial and group-like comodules (TauCeti#101), the regular
comodule (TauCeti#122), corestriction along a coalgebra morphism (TauCeti#97), transport across a
linear equivalence (TauCeti#109), and cofree comodules together with the universal property that
comodule morphisms into M ⊗[R] C are just linear maps into M
(Comodule.Hom.cofreeEquiv,
TauCeti#129). The subobject theory is now reasonably complete: the lattice of subcomodules
(TauCeti#136), inverse images and kernels (TauCeti#241), the induced coaction on the subtype of a
subcomodule (TauCeti#909), quotients with their lift and its uniqueness (TauCeti#785), and on the
coalgebra side subcoalgebra suprema and finiteness (TauCeti#124), images (TauCeti#127), spans of
group-like elements (TauCeti#119), and the order embedding of subcoalgebras into subcomodules of
the regular comodule (TauCeti#138). Over a bialgebra the diagonal tensor product of comodules was
assembled (TauCeti#890, TauCeti#1027) and then restricted to the finitely generated ones, which
now form a monoidal category
(FGComoduleCat.instMonoidalCategory,
TauCeti#1280 and TauCeti#1321). Monoidal, not rigid: there are no duals of comodules here, and
none of the results the roadmap actually wants from this layer, the finite-dimensional
subcoalgebra theorem, faithfulness, the embedding theorem into GLₙ, or Tannakian reconstruction,
have been attempted.

The Hopf-ideal lane advanced in parallel and stayed at the Hopf-algebra level. A bialgebra
morphism killing a two-sided coideal factors uniquely through the quotient bialgebra
(TauCeti#237); the kernel of a surjective bialgebra morphism is a Hopf ideal, and the quotient by
it is bialgebra-equivalent to the codomain
(HopfIdeal.kerLiftBialgEquiv,
TauCeti#185); and Hopf ideals pull back along surjections compatibly with the lattice operations
(TauCeti#383). Around these sit the Layer 0 supports: the convolution group structure on
H →ₐ[R] A with inverse f ↦ f ∘ S
(AlgHom.instGroup,
TauCeti#45) and its packaging as a functor in the value algebra (TauCeti#54), the points of a
tensor product as the product of the points (TauCeti#167, made natural in TauCeti#458), the points
of the trivial group (TauCeti#428), the Hopf-algebra structure on a symmetric algebra with
antipode ι x ↦ -ι x (TauCeti#165), the monoid algebra of a product as a tensor product of
monoid algebras (TauCeti#297), the universal property of a free abelian character group
(TauCeti#282), restriction of scalars on CommAlgCat (TauCeti#762), and a coordinate-ring functor
from finitely generated commutative groups to finite-type commutative Hopf algebras
(DiagonalizableGroup.coordinateRingFunctor,
TauCeti#1214), which is one direction of the Layer 4 anti-equivalence and not yet the equivalence.
Matrix coefficients also got their first multiplicativity statements: the coefficient submodule of
a tensor product of comodules contains the product of the two coefficient submodules (TauCeti#1139).

Proportion is worth stating plainly. Of the hundred pull requests in this window, fifty-five added
no new declarations at all; they split modules into directories, renamed, adjusted imports, and
consolidated. Of the rest, a large share is the routine _apply, _comp, and _toLinearMap
plumbing that makes the comodule API usable. One other design point is visible throughout the
declaration list: everything is stated over a general commutative base ring R rather than over a
field, so the field-specific parts of the roadmap, geometric connectedness, smoothness, and
anything defined after base change to k̄, remain untouched.

Full log: https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups/PROGRESS.md
progress-log-id:ReductiveGroups-1f1d752-ed837d5

Oh this is an interesting experiment! It could definitely have been made about 3x as short though, if it was supposed to be human-readable (I would write a summary of the summary myself but I'm stuck on mobile at the minute --i am assuming this was AI-generated)
I will pass that along. :-)
(These progress logs will be posted about once a day, and will select whichever roadmap has had the most progress since its last progress report.)

Exchangeability — progress on 105 merged pull requests (c484d4c to 6919462)

De Finetti's theorem landed. deFinetti (TauCeti#1444) says that an exchangeable process valued in a nonempty standard Borel space is conditionally i.i.d., and deFinetti_RyllNardzewski_equivalence (<https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Probability/DeFinetti/Theorem.html#TauCeti.Probability.deFinetti_RyllNardzewski_equivalence>) closes the triangle: contractable iff exchangeable and conditionally i.i.d. The conclusion is the strong one the roadmap asked for, the joint-law disintegration of (ν, block) as ∫ δ_{ν ω} ⊗ (ν ω)^{⊗m}, not merely the mixture identity; the hard direction is conditionallyIID_of_contractable (TauCeti#1395), reached by the reverse-martingale route. Uniqueness came with it, both a.e. uniqueness of the directing measure (TauCeti#1430) and uniqueness of the mixing law (TauCeti#1277), as did the unique-mixture form (TauCeti#1462) and the extension to arbitrary countably infinite index types (TauCeti#1451).

Two theorems of independent interest arrived on the way, neither mentioning exchangeability. Lévy's downward theorem, tendsto_ae_condExp_iInf (<https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Probability/Martingale/Convergence.html#MeasureTheory.tendsto_ae_condExp_iInf>), gives a.s. and L¹ convergence of μ[f | 𝔽ₙ] along an arbitrary decreasing filtration (TauCeti#1031), assembled from a finite-horizon time reversal of Mathlib's upcrossing bound (TauCeti#686, TauCeti#734). And the Hewitt–Savage zero-one law (TauCeti#1199), next to a careful separation of the tail, shift-invariant, and exchangeable σ-algebras, with an explicit Bool-valued path event witnessing that the tail is not contained in the shift-invariant σ-algebra (TauCeti#1175).

The other two proof routes are unfinished. The Koopman lane is complete as operator theory, up to identifying the mean-ergodic projection with conditional expectation given the invariant σ-algebra (TauCeti#1351, TauCeti#1408), but no deFinetti_viaKoopman is stated; the L² lane has its uniform covariance structure and block-average estimates (TauCeti#788, TauCeti#1097) and stops at Cesàro L¹ convergence, short of deFinetti_viaL2. Much of the remaining window is product-kernel and cylinder API feeding the common endings.

Full log: https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/Exchangeability/PROGRESS.md
progress-log-id:Exchangeability-c484d4c-6919462

Thanks for setting this up!

I took a closer look at TauCetiRoadmap#128 about the Exchangeability roadmap. The PROGRESS.md file seemed fine, but the STATUS.md had a bunch of overclaims and other things worth correcting, which I've tried to address in TauCetiRoadmap#129.

Maybe we should have automated frequent progress updates, but make the status updates subject to at least adversarial AI review (or potentially human review and a slower pace, more like the roadmaps themselves)?
Thanks, I'll look at this tomorrow. Yes: if STATUS.md is being updated inaccurately, we definitely need to be more careful, as implementing agents will look at this and go in the wrong direction.
@Cameron Freer, in TauCetiRoadmap#129, you are modifying the roadmap as well as correcting the status report. Please separate these!

Sorry about that -- I'll fix it

[update: fixed. TauCetiRoadmap#129 now has just the update to STATUS.md; the changes it had incorporated from TauCetiRoadmap#99 are now gone, and TauCetiRoadmap#99 is reopened.]

ContourIntegration — progress on 92 merged pull requests (5d29c9d to 6919462)

The summit landed. hungerbuhlerWasem_residueTheorem (TauCeti#966) is HW Thm 3.3: for f holomorphic on U ∖ S and meromorphic at each point of a finite S, and a null-homologous closed piecewise-C¹ immersion that may pass through the singularities, the Cauchy principal value of ∮ f is 2πi · Σ_s n_s(γ) · Res_s f, weighted by the generalized non-integer winding numbers <https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Contour/HungerbuhlerWasem.html#TauCeti.Contour.hungerbuhlerWasem_residueTheorem>. Conditions (A′) and (B) enter as hypotheses; at simple poles both are automatic (TauCeti#972, TauCeti#1205), so that regime is unconditional, and its one-point winding-½ case is the half-residue πi · Res_s f.

The classical backbone arrived in the same window: the homology Cauchy theorem, by Dixon's argument (TauCeti#911, TauCeti#919) <https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Contour/HomologyCauchy.html#TauCeti.Contour.homologyCauchyTheorem>, its integral formula for f and for every iterated derivative (TauCeti#1464), the classical residue theorem for a null-homologous cycle avoiding its poles (TauCeti#1439), and the argument principle counting zeros and poles by winding weight (TauCeti#1463).

Underneath, the winding number acquired its geometry — the model sector's α/2π, hence ½ at a smooth crossing and 1/6 at a π/3 corner (TauCeti#1385, TauCeti#705), and the circle's 1 inside, 0 outside (TauCeti#967, TauCeti#1203). The worked examples close the loop, notably the principal value of e^{iaz}/z along [−R, R] tending to πi (TauCeti#1271) <https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Contour/WorkedExamples/HalfDisc/Dirichlet.html#TauCeti.Contour.tendsto_cauchyPV_realSegment_dirichlet>. Two gaps deserve naming: HW Prop 2.3's real bounded-integrand formula is proved only off the curve (TauCeti#962), with the crossing value (ẋÿ − ẏẍ)/(2(ẋ² + ẏ²)) separate and under a C² hypothesis (TauCeti#1488); and homotopy invariance is stated for C² homotopies (TauCeti#1364). About a fifth of the pull requests here added no declarations at all — module splits and proof consolidation.

Full log: https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/ContourIntegration/PROGRESS.md
progress-log-id:ContourIntegration-5d29c9d-6919462

@Kim Morrison I've now separated the PRs for updating the status report (TauCetiRoadmap#129) and the roadmap correction (TauCetiRoadmap#99, now reopened). I agree that this makes sense, and I'll avoid combining such changes in the future.

The reason I had initially combined them is that one of the things that the original TauCetiRoadmap#128 status update got wrong was based on reading a stale README (which the open TauCetiRoadmap#99 had aimed to correct). While it doesn't seem reasonable to expect a status report bot to incorporate content from unreviewed open PRs, in this case the content of TauCetiRoadmap#99 was based on a recent TauCeti PR (TauCeti#1277) that had landed after adversarial AI review -- maybe there's some way to fast-track roadmap revisions that are based on decisions made in such PRs?

(I expect that this situation will be pretty common, where it is discovered (by either the author agent or review agent) that the roadmap result is true but in fact holds under weaker hypotheses. Especially in cases where the only way for the PR to pass review is to prove something stronger than the stated roadmap result, it may make sense to have a quick mechanism for updating the roadmap so that later agents aren't misled.)

RepresentationTheory — progress on 89 merged pull requests (7435a81 to 6919462)

The finite-group spine reached its structure theorem: over an algebraically closed field whose
characteristic does not divide the order, k[G] is a product of matrix algebras, the blocks are
indexed by the conjugacy classes, and the squares of the matrix sizes sum to |G| (TauCeti#1360)
<https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/CharacterTable/Wedderburn.html#TauCeti.exists_algEquiv_pi_matrix>.
Under it sit the general algebra results it needs: the double centralizer theorem with
Jacobson-Chevalley density (TauCeti#1435), and Wedderburn-Artin for central simple algebras together
with the centrality and simplicity of tensor products (TauCeti#1472, TauCeti#1548, TauCeti#1625).
On the analytic side, Weyl's unitarian trick
<https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Compact/Unitarizable.html#TauCeti.ContRepresentation.isUnitarizable>
and complete reducibility for unitary representations arrived (TauCeti#1532, TauCeti#1440), and
induction acquired Frobenius reciprocity as a character identity (TauCeti#1476)
<https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Induction/FrobeniusReciprocity.html#TauCeti.frobenius_reciprocity>.

Several other lanes advanced by building vocabulary rather than theorems. Quiver representations
gained the path algebra, vertex simples, the indecomposable projectives and injectives with their
dimension vectors, and the Euler and Tits forms with the vertex reflections preserving them
(TauCeti#1437, TauCeti#1494, TauCeti#1528). The symmetric-group lane built row and column groups,
Young symmetrizers, the key vanishing lemma, and the left ideals they generate, whose character
depends only on the shape of the tableau (TauCeti#1403, TauCeti#1480, TauCeti#1458). Root systems
got inversions and the exchange count, the Coxeter matrix of a base, and the Dynkin types with their
standard Cartan matrices (TauCeti#1263, TauCeti#1483, TauCeti#1431). Projective representation
theory started at the bottom, with factor sets, the extensions they build and are recovered from,
and the twisted group algebra (TauCeti#1588, TauCeti#1637, TauCeti#1596).

Much of the rest is scaffolding, and two named targets landed only in part: hook lengths are defined
and related to transposition, but the hook-length formula is proved only for a single row or column
(TauCeti#1496), and compact-group Schur orthogonality appears only in its cross-representation half
(TauCeti#1568).

Full log: https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/PROGRESS.md
progress-log-id:RepresentationTheory-7435a81-6919462

ConformalMapping — progress on 75 merged pull requests (160fbce to 6919462)

The Riemann mapping theorem landed: every nonempty, simply connected, open proper subset of ℂ
admits a holomorphic bijection onto the unit disc (TauCeti#1346,
<https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/Conformal/RiemannMapping/Existence.html#TauCeti.riemannMapping>),
with a normalized form sending a chosen base point to 0 with positive real derivative, unique as
such (TauCeti#1500), uniqueness up to a disc automorphism (TauCeti#1335), and the corollary that any
two simply connected proper domains are conformally equivalent (TauCeti#1519). It was assembled in
the standard order rather than imported: the family of pointed disc injections is nonempty by the
square-root trick and normal by Montel's selection theorem (TauCeti#1226,
<https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/Conformal/Montel.html#TauCeti.montel>),
the extremal problem has a maximizer (TauCeti#1326), and the maximizer omits nothing (TauCeti#1343).

The layers under and over the summit came with it. Under: Rouché, Hurwitz, Morera as named
theorems, Vitali, the open-mapping degree (TauCeti#1209, TauCeti#1520, TauCeti#1585); Schwarz–Pick
in contraction, infinitesimal and rigidity forms, the Poincaré disc as a proper geodesic space whose
geodesics through the origin are exactly the Euclidean diameters, and Aut(𝔻) as a transitively
acting group (TauCeti#752, TauCeti#1512, TauCeti#1502). Over: Schwarz reflection across the real
axis (TauCeti#1091,
<https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/Conformal/Reflection/Principle.html#TauCeti.differentiableOn_schwarzReflection_of_symmetric>),
then across a line, an analytic arc and a circle, with Painlevé removability and injectivity of the
reflected map (TauCeti#1243, TauCeti#1377, TauCeti#1565), and the monodromy theorem (TauCeti#1558).

Carathéodory is the open layer, and only its converse direction is proved: a conformal map with an
injective continuous extension makes its domain a Jordan domain (TauCeti#1580), together with the
"only if" half of the continuity theorem (TauCeti#1587). The extension itself is not established;
what landed towards it is machinery — cluster sets, uniformly locally connected boundaries, the area
formula (TauCeti#1555, TauCeti#1624, TauCeti#1583). Schwarz–Christoffel is untouched. Per the
roadmap's own coordination clause, the L0–L3 material is a shim to be retired once the Mathlib proof
lands.

Full log: https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/ConformalMapping/PROGRESS.md
progress-log-id:ConformalMapping-160fbce-6919462

Multiquadratic — progress on 73 merged pull requests (1d6c6f4 to 6919462)

The degree theorem is in place: under square-class independence of the radicands (no nonempty subset product a square in K), [K(√d₁,…,√dₙ) : K] = 2ⁿ (TauCeti#146, TauCeti#147), together with the square-class descent engine it rests on. The Galois side followed: the extension is Galois, an automorphism is determined by its sign pattern on the generators, and the group has exponent exactly two and order 2ⁿ (TauCeti#150, TauCeti#277, TauCeti#997). Relative degrees and relative Galois groups over an intermediate field are read off the attached 𝔽₂-subspace (TauCeti#965, TauCeti#1434), and the subfield lattice is counted for prime radicands (TauCeti#424).

The splitting law arrived through Frobenius elements: an arithmetic Frobenius at an odd prime p acts on a square root of d by legendreSym p d, so the Frobenius of a multiquadratic field is the vector of Legendre symbols and is trivial exactly when every radicand is a residue mod p (TauCeti#1056, TauCeti#173) — stated away from the ramified primes, as the roadmap asks. Alongside it, Cl/Cl² was built as the maximal elementary-2 quotient, kept distinct from Cl[2] while proved equinumerous with it (TauCeti#294, TauCeti#555), with the exact unit-square index 2^(rank+1) (TauCeti#1038) and quadratic conjugation shown to invert ideal classes, hence to act trivially on Cl/Cl² (TauCeti#1631).

Toward the summit, the compositum of the prime-discriminant quadratic fields dividing the discriminant of ℚ(√d) now exists, with degree 2ᵗ over ℚ, containing √d, and of degree 2^(t-1) over that base with even-parity sign group (TauCeti#1366, TauCeti#1389, TauCeti#1639). It is named the candidate genus field, and honestly so: nothing yet identifies it with the maximal unramified extension abelian over ℚ, and neither Gal(K_gen/K) ≅ Cl/Cl² nor the 2-rank formula is touched. Much of the rest was fundamental-discriminant arithmetic (TauCeti#1045, TauCeti#1095) and file reorganisation.

Full log: https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/Multiquadratic/PROGRESS.md
progress-log-id:Multiquadratic-1d6c6f4-6919462

HeegaardFloer — progress on 66 merged pull requests (e642cc5 to 6919462)

Lane F0 acquired a working theory of Fredholm operators, which the roadmap lists first among the things nothing existed for. The index is defined and shown additive under composition (TauCeti#1294) and Cartesian products (TauCeti#1113), zero for bijections and for self-adjoint operators (TauCeti#1329), and negated by passing to the adjoint (TauCeti#1381); over Banach spaces the closed-range condition turns out not to be independent, so Fredholmness reduces to finite-dimensional kernel and cokernel (TauCeti#1147). The useful half is stability: the Fredholm operators of a given index form an open set (TauCeti#1349), and the index of a continuous family is locally constant, hence constant along paths and on preconnected parameter sets (TauCeti#1608, <https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Fredholm/ContinuousFamily.html#TauCeti.Continuous.isLocallyConstant_index>).

Lane F2.1's definitions landed in bulk, in linear form: symplectic forms with tameness, invariance and compatibility, the associated metric, the Hermitian inner product of a compatible pair (TauCeti#341), transport and symplectomorphisms (TauCeti#265, TauCeti#613), and the linear cotangent space with its zero section and fibre Lagrangian for the canonical form and maximal totally real for the canonical J (TauCeti#1213, TauCeti#1595). Totally real subspaces got their own file, with the half-dimension count and the implication the roadmap actually wants, that a Lagrangian of a taming pair is maximal totally real (TauCeti#286, TauCeti#1046, <https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Geometry/Symplectic/Lagrangian/TotallyReal.html#TauCeti.SymplecticForm.IsLagrangian.isMaximalTotallyReal_of_tames>). J-holomorphicity is stated for varying almost complex structures, with the chain rule (TauCeti#1206, <https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Geometry/Symplectic/JHolomorphic/Varying.html#TauCeti.IsJHolomorphic>).

All of this is pointwise and linear: there are no symplectic manifolds, no energy, and no moduli spaces yet. Sard is still absent, so Sard–Smale and transversality have not begun, and Sym^g exists only as the bijection between unordered tuples and monic polynomials (TauCeti#1469).

Full log: https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer/PROGRESS.md
progress-log-id:HeegaardFloer-e642cc5-6919462

UniversalCovers — progress on 63 merged pull requests (1099f3b to 11ef09d)

The universal cover is now constructed here rather than assumed. Based paths out of x₀,
modulo endpoint-preserving homotopy, carry a quotient topology whose endpoint projection is a
covering map, with path-connected and simply connected total space and the expected unique
lifting property, under the roadmap's standing hypotheses on the base (TauCeti#993,
TauCeti#1104, TauCeti#1208,
<https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/UniversalCover/Covering.html#TauCeti.UniversalCover.isCoveringMap>);
the discreteness of homotopy-class fibres that makes this work came first (TauCeti#990). The
convention question the roadmap flagged resolved against the naive form: with π₁(X, x₀) acting
on the left by prepending inverse loops, the deck group of the projection is the opposite
fundamental group (TauCeti#1594,
<https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/UniversalCover/Deck/FundamentalGroup/UniversalCover.html#TauCeti.UniversalCover.deckFundamentalGroupEquiv>).

The classification arrived in both forms. Pointed connected covers of (X, x₀) are classified by
the subgroup of π₁(X, x₀) they recover (TauCeti#1581,
<https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/UniversalCover/Classification/Pointed.html#TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.exists_homeomorph_comp_eq_iff_range_eq>),
unpointed ones by its conjugacy class (TauCeti#1600), and a cover is regular exactly when that
subgroup is normal (TauCeti#1630). The existence half is less finished than that sounds: the
quotient UniversalCover x₀ / H is built and recovers exactly H (TauCeti#1603, TauCeti#1797),
but nothing here records its descended projection as a covering map, and the deck group N(H)/H
is present only as group-theoretic scaffolding (TauCeti#600, TauCeti#749).

Higher homotopy came with it: covering maps induce isomorphisms on π_n for n ≥ 2
(TauCeti#1189), over functoriality, product and invariance API for π_n written from scratch
(TauCeti#765, TauCeti#1400). That gives π_n(S¹) = 0 for n ≥ 2, and circles and tori as
K(G, 1) spaces (TauCeti#1219, TauCeti#1468). Real projective space arrived as the antipodal
quotient with a two-element deck group (TauCeti#1679, TauCeti#1747), but π₁(RPⁿ) is not
established: that needs Sⁿ simply connected, which is not here. A third of this window's pull
requests added no new declarations at all.

Full log: https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/UniversalCovers/PROGRESS.md
progress-log-id:UniversalCovers-1099f3b-11ef09d

CombinatorialHeegaardFloer — progress on 60 merged pull requests (06f94e6 to 11ef09d)

Grid diagrams acquired their move calculus, and with it links. Commutation of non-interleaving adjacent rows or columns, stabilization splitting an O- or X-marking, and their inverses are now a single reversible relation IsMove; a grid link is the quotient of grid diagrams of every size by the equivalence it generates, and two diagrams present the same link exactly when moves connect them, with GridLink.lift turning move-invariant functions on diagrams into functions on links (TauCeti#1589). The roadmap's convention that a link is a grid diagram modulo grid moves is now a definition, so nothing downstream waits on Cromwell's theorem.

Two standard families arrived: the unknot grid of every size, and torusLink for the (p+1, q+1) torus link, both with the gradings of their marked states. finite-type Hopf algebra over a field is a torus exactly when it is of multiplicative type,
geometrically connected and geometrically reduced.

Layer 5 opened with the geometric definition of unipotence, verified for 𝔾ₐ and the
upper-unitriangular groups and stable under products, quotients and extensions; such a group
has no nontrivial characters. Reductivity and
semisimplicity exist only as properties so far: no group has been proved reductive, and there
is no unipotent radical, no Lie-Kolchin theorem and no Borel theory beyond GL₂. Separately,
the Chevalley lane built the Serre presentation of split semisimple Lie algebras, the rank-one
Kostant form, and root subgroups of GLₙ and SLₙ satisfying the type-A commutator relations.

RepresentationTheory — progress on 147 merged pull requests (671091a to dfa452e)

The Cartan–Killing classification is now complete: every irreducible reduced crystallographic finite root system has a unique valid Dynkin type. The existence side is concrete as well, with a pinned simply connected root datum for every valid type, including the previously missing types B, F₄, E₇ and E₈.

The Pin and Spin actions were assembled as double covers with kernel ℤ/2. These statements require a positive-dimensional finite nondegenerate quadratic space over a separably closed field with 2 invertible; over a general field, the image of Spin is instead identified with the kernel of the spinor norm.

Highest-weight theory now shows that every finite-dimensional irreducible module has a unique dominant integral highest weight, and the Casimir element is central. This is not yet the highest-weight classification: Verma modules and the irreducible quotients L(λ) have not landed. Supporting lanes added the Bruhat decomposition of GL₂ and the Bender–Knuth involutions.

ModularForms — progress on 104 merged pull requests (5c3a971 to 113fad8)

The level-one valence formula is now proved: for a nonzero weight-k form, the cusp order, half the order at i, a third of the order at ρ, and the orders on the remaining orbits sum to k/12. The same work established finite support for the divisor and developed the full-coset norm machinery needed at general level, but the general-level formula itself has not landed.

The Hecke development now turns an arbitrary double coset for (Γ₁(N), Δ₀(N)) into a linear endomorphism of modular forms, with the corresponding operator on cusp forms. At bad primes, the upper-triangular part preserves nebentypus and has coefficient a_{pm}(f); the diagonal contribution needed at good primes is also computed. This is not yet the uniform T_n action or a Hecke-ring homomorphism, and the augmented prime sum is not yet identified with the full T_p double coset. On the structural side, Shimura's polynomial presentation at rank two is complete, while general rank remains open.

The Petersson product is now unitary under diamond operators, making distinct nebentypus components orthogonal. Consequently the old/new decomposition restricts to each character space. The exact conductor-indexed description of the oldspace and Hecke stability, especially at bad primes, remain to be proved.
